clue.text: Having eaten nothing, Liza began to prepare dessert

indicators.note: something that has eaten another thing holds it inside, so one piece goes within the other
to prepare a dish is to work its ingredients into shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: nothing is zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A woman called Liza starts making a pudding on an empty stomach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to prepare' rearranges LIZA BEGAN into ZABAGLINE, and 'Having eaten' puts O (nothing) inside it before the final NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Zabaglione is an Italian whipped custard of egg yolks, sugar and wine, served as a sweet course.

clue.text: African animal park facilities discussed

indicators.note: something discussed is spoken about, so the clue works by how the words sound when said

parts.note: an animal park is a zoo and its facilities are its loo, the British word for a toilet

explanation.surface: Talk about an African creature and the amenities at a wildlife park.
explanation.walkthrough: LOO is everyday British for a toilet, so the zoo's 'facilities' are a ZOO LOO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Zulu are a people of southern Africa, so a Zulu is an African person.

clue.text: Knock second-class referee, one about to retire

parts.note: B is the grade for second class, after A

indicators.note: to retire is to withdraw, so these pieces leave the word they were in

parts.note: an umpire is a referee in games such as cricket and tennis
I is the Roman numeral for one
re means about or concerning, as in a letter heading

explanation.surface: A sports official knocks a lesser referee who is about to stop working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retire' takes I (one) and RE (about) out of UMPIRE, leaving UMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A bump is a knock or jolt, as when a car bumps into another.

clue.text: Ordered research into flipping male individuals entering uninvited

indicators.note: one piece is put into another, so it sits inside it
flipping something turns it over, so this word is read backwards

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is men only

indicators.note: letters that are ordered are put in a new arrangement, so these are shuffled

explanation.surface: Research into flipping men who barge in where they're not wanted was commissioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild curse but turns the male deer backwards; 'Ordered' scrambles the research, and 'into' sets that scramble inside the reversed word, before its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Gatecrashers are people who turn up at a party or event without an invitation.

clue.text: Know instinctively trendy tourist goes missing every so often

parts.note: in means fashionable or trendy

indicators.note: every other letter of this word drops out, leaving the alternate ones

explanation.surface: You just know the fashionable traveller keeps disappearing from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes missing every so often' strikes out the 2nd, 4th and 6th letters of TOURIST, leaving TUIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To intuit something is to grasp it by feeling rather than by reasoning.

clue.text: New politician unusually alone visits leading light in advertising?

indicators.note: one who visits goes into a place, so these letters go inside the other pieces

parts.note: MP stands for Member of Parliament

indicators.note: doing something unusually means in an odd way, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A newly elected politician, unusually on their own, calls on a leading figure in the ad world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leading light' looks like a star ad executive; it is a literal glowing sign. 'unusually' scrambles 'alone' and 'visits' sets the result between the new and the politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon lamps glow brightly in shop signs and billboards, so they are literally the lights of advertising.

clue.text: Wife assumes husband's role in store to barter

indicators.note: taking over a role means one letter stands in for another in the word
a part played in the word by one letter is now played by another

parts.note: a shop is a store
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife takes over her husband's job in the shop so as to trade.
explanation.walkthrough: W (wife) replaces H (husband) in SHOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Swop is a variant spelling of swap, to exchange one thing for another, which is what bartering is.

clue.text: Less than generous, the support for Western child prodigy

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits below, so the other pieces come under the first

parts.note: under means less than, as in under ten
kind means generous

explanation.surface: A stingy remark about propping up the Western, said of a gifted youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Less than generous' reads as stingy, but it is UNDER KIND; 'the support for' puts both beneath W in the down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wunderkind is German for wonder child, used in English for a young person of startling talent.

clue.text: Ripped abs helped to carry originally bulky wallcovering

indicators.note: one piece carries another by holding it inside
ripped means torn apart, so these letters are pulled into a new order
originally means at the start, so the first letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: Muscular abdominal work helped someone haul a heavy wall finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ripped' looks like slang for muscular; it is the anagram signal for ABS HELPED. 'to carry' puts B, the start of 'bulky', inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Pebbledash is a coating of render studded with small stones, applied to outside walls of British houses.

clue.text: Lack of talent in legislature essentially attracting mockery

indicators.note: the essence of a word is its very centre, so the middle letter is taken

parts.note: an imitation can be a mockery, a poor copy that mocks the real thing

explanation.surface: A legislature, at heart, is criticised for its incompetence and draws ridicule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essentially' takes L, the middle letter of the eleven in LEGISLATURE, and 'attracting' joins it to IMITATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A limitation is a shortcoming in ability, a point beyond which one's talent does not reach.

clue.text: Poet runs away over humiliation

indicators.note: turned over means flipped round, so these letters are read backwards
something sent away is taken out, so this letter leaves the word

parts.note: Robert Burns is Scotland's national poet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A poet runs off because he has been humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes R (runs) from BURNS to give BUNS, and 'over' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: A snub is a deliberate slight or rebuff, a small public humiliation.

clue.text: Key defender, star who's bound to draw crowds?

definitions.text: star who's bound to draw crowds?

parts.note: Esc is the escape key on a computer keyboard
an apologist is someone who defends a cause or argument

explanation.surface: A key defender in a team is the star player sure to pull in the fans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound' looks like 'certain'; here it means tied up, which is how an escapologist starts the act.
explanation.definitionFit: An escapologist, like Houdini, is a performer who wriggles free of chains and ropes, attracting big audiences.

clue.text: After a cold, there's something slippery about that woman exhibiting weakness

indicators.note: after means following, so what follows is placed later in the answer

parts.note: a chill is a cold, a mild illness

indicators.note: about means around, so one word wraps round the other

parts.note: an eel is notoriously slippery
she refers to that woman

explanation.surface: After catching a cold, a woman shows a weakness for something slippery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' fixes the order, so the slippery part comes after the cold; 'about' has the fish wrapped round the woman, giving ESHEEL.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Achilles could only be wounded in his heel, so the phrase means a fatal weak spot.

clue.text: Time a car crashed overtaking empty Mazda on cracked, raised road surface

indicators.note: overtaking here means taking over, so these letters surround the next piece
a crashed car is wrecked, so these letters are jumbled
an empty word loses its insides, leaving just its first and last letters
in a down answer, raised means read upwards, so this word is reversed

parts.note: cracked means mad, crazy

explanation.surface: A car crash in which the driver passes an empty Mazda on a damaged, raised road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crashed' scrambles 'a car' into ARCA, 'overtaking' wraps it round the empty car's shell, and 'raised' reads the cracked word upwards, as suits a down answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarmacadam is crushed stone bound with tar, laid as the surface of roads.

clue.text: One was previously fired and removed from comedy act

indicators.note: removing a word from a name takes it out, leaving the rest

parts.note: Cannon and Ball were a popular British comedy double act of the 1980s

explanation.surface: Someone was sacked and dropped from a comedy routine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' looks like sacked, but a cannonball was shot from a gun. CANNON AND BALL were a British TV comedy duo; 'removed from' takes out AND.
explanation.definitionFit: Cannonballs were solid iron shot launched by cannons in earlier centuries, now rarely used.

clue.text: Computer image of some aristocrat available to review

indicators.note: to review is to look back over, so these letters are read backwards
some of these words means a run of letters taken from inside them

explanation.surface: A picture on screen of an aristocrat, available for viewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes RATAVA from aristoCRAT AVAilable and 'to review' reads it backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An avatar is the picture or figure representing a user in a game or on a website.

clue.text: Went aboard British vessel entering eastern Mediterranean

indicators.note: something entering goes inside, so these letters sit within the others

parts.note: Med is the short form of the Mediterranean Sea
an ark is a vessel, as in Noah's Ark

explanation.surface: A British ship sails into the eastern Mediterranean and people climb on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entering' sets the British vessel inside the pair of abbreviations, splitting eastern from Mediterranean although the clue names the vessel first.
explanation.definitionFit: To embark is to board a ship or aircraft, so embarked means went aboard.

clue.text: Minimise parking in front of store

indicators.note: in front of means before, so this piece comes first in the answer

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for parking, as on road signs
to lay down wine is to store it for later

explanation.surface: Keep it small by parking outside the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'store' looks like a shop; it is a verb, as in laying down wine in a cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: To play something down is to make it seem less important than it is.

clue.text: Half of city starts to isolate local delinquent boy

indicators.note: half of a word is taken, here its front five letters

parts.note: Manchester is a major city in north-west England

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: Half a city's young people start to cut off a neighbourhood tearaway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'delinquent boy' reads as one phrase, but 'delinquent' gives only its D; the definition is 'boy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Man-child is a literary word for a boy, a male child, as Wordsworth used it.

clue.text: Finishes off sandwiches

definitions.meaning: to round off or ... something is to complete it
a round is a sandwich made from two whole slices of bread

explanation.definitionFit: Rounds off means completes, and in Britain a round of sandwiches is one sandwich of two full slices.

clue.text: Public library interrupted by oddly loud roar, or roars perhaps?

indicators.note: a word interrupted by others has them inserted into it
oddly means the odd-numbered letters are taken

explanation.surface: A quiet public library is disturbed by a loud roar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' keeps the 1st, 3rd, 5th and 7th letters of the loud roar, and 'interrupted by' splits the library abbreviation to take them in. The question mark flags a definition by example.
explanation.definitionFit: Roars is an example of a plural noun, the many-form of roar.

clue.text: Norwich City footballer with faint-hearted tone

parts.note: Norwich City, an English football club, are nicknamed the Canaries
yellow means cowardly

explanation.surface: A Norwich City player who lacks courage.
explanation.walkthrough: Norwich City play in yellow and are known as the Canaries, so each player is a CANARY.
explanation.definitionFit: Canary yellow is a bright shade of yellow, a colour or tone named after the bird.

clue.text: Reportedly get on fine …

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the clue works by sound

parts.note: to fare is to get on, as in how did you fare

explanation.surface: It is said someone is getting along well.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis runs this clue into the next, but each stands alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair weather is fine weather: dry and bright.

clue.text: … with character Mike is succeeding, large Eddy

parts.note: Mike is M in the radio alphabet, and the letter it follows is L, written out as el

explanation.surface: Mike the character is doing well, large Eddy says.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter before M is L, and 'character' asks for its name spelled out: EL.
explanation.definitionFit: A well can mean a swirl or upwelling of water, and Chambers lists eddy as a sense.

clue.text: Italy, not part of theoretical agreement

indicators.note: not being part of a word means being taken out of it

parts.note: ideal can mean existing only in theory or in the mind
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: Italy is not part of a deal that exists only on paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not part of' takes I (Italy) out of IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A deal is an agreement, a bargain struck between parties.

clue.text: Match broadcast on radio, etc

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: A sports fixture is carried on the radio and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Match' looks like a fixture being broadcast; it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To coordinate colours or clothes is to make them match or go together.

clue.text: Distance from motorway, Alex discovered?

parts.note: the M1 is Britain's first motorway, written here as MI

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the cover off, so the outer letters go, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: How far is it from the motorway, as Alex found out?
explanation.walkthrough: The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds; read as letters it gives MI. 'discovered' strips ALEX to LE.
explanation.definitionFit: A mile is a unit of distance, 1,760 yards.

clue.text: On one side of college, student welcoming former artist

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so these letters go inside the others

parts.note: uni is short for university, a college
L is for learner, a student driver
late means former, as in the late president
RA stands for Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: On one side of the college, a student is greeting a former artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'welcoming' has the college and student together take in the former artist, so the student's L ends the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Unilateral means affecting or carried out by one side or party only.
